Druskininkai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Alytus County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Druskininkai, Lithuania's oldest spa town, saw Jews settle from the mid-18th century, reaching about half the population (636 of 1,280) by 1897; a hospital and charity house for impoverished Jews was established in 1853. Among those buried here was Rachele Leah Krinski Lipchitz, mother of the renowned Litvak sculptor Jacques Lipchitz, a major figure of Cubist sculpture; the family's hotel, run by Lipchitz's father Abraham, survives today, and the small building where the young artist spent his childhood became a museum in 1996. About 800 of Druskininkai's Jews were driven into a ghetto after the German occupation in 1941, later deported via the Kolbasin concentration camp near Grodno to the Treblinka death camp. This cemetery, consecrated in the 1880s alongside the founding of the town's Jewish community, was demolished in 1967.
